title: A max value of 0 means both 'unlimited' and 'zero' in the same Cap Automator table
content:
The `max` parameter is defined at A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.1.3.1.3 as "the maximum the Supply Cap or Borrow Cap can be increased to." In the live configurations it takes the value 0 with two contradictory meanings.

Unlimited: USDC (A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.1.3.2.6), USDT (.3.2.7) and pyUSD (.3.2.15) each record `max: 0 (no cap)` for both supply and borrow — the parenthetical is doing all the work, encoding 0 as a sentinel for "no ceiling."

Zero: sDai (.3.2.5) records `max: 0 sDAI` under a borrow cap annotated "n/a - not a borrowable asset" — here 0 means literally none.

Read strictly by the definition, `max: 0` should mean a cap that cannot be raised above zero. Under that reading, USDT's supply cap could never exceed 0 — plainly not the intent for the largest stablecoin market. Only the free-text annotations disambiguate, and the neighbouring entries show the alternative convention was available: wstETH and rETH express "effectively disabled" as `max: 1 wstETH` / `max: 1 rETH` (.3.2.2, .3.2.3), and WETH expresses unlimited as the word `Unlimited` (.3.2.1).

So the Artifact contains at least three encodings for the same two concepts, with the disambiguating information carried in prose rather than in the value. For a document whose purpose is to be the authoritative record of on-chain risk limits, a sentinel that inverts meaning between adjacent rows is a real defect — a reader or downstream tool applying the stated definition uniformly would get the largest markets exactly backwards.
description: USDC, USDT and pyUSD record max: 0 (no cap) while sDai records max: 0 sDAI meaning not borrowable — identical values with opposite meanings in adjacent subdocuments.
